text:
Alex H: heads-up: seeing surges of connection resets to S3 from model-serving fleet in us-west-2. CloudWatch shows NAT GW ephemeral ports near exhaustion (~78% reuse). Started ~08:12 PT.

oncall-bot: ALERT: NATGW_EPHEMERAL_PORTS_HIGH us-west-2 - AvailablePorts=1200 (threshold=200) - triggered at 08:15 PT

Julia R: looks like a lot of short lived outbound sockets from replicas during concurrent model pulls + health pings. Any recent deploys that increase parallel pulls?

Sam T: Noted. Quick mitigations: 1) add EIPs to NATGW (fast, but costly), 2) route heavy S3 traffic via VPC Gateway Endpoint (avoids SNAT), 3) deploy an egress-proxy with connection pooling (keep-alive), 4) spin up NAT instance fleet with connection tracking tuned. Recommend (2) + (3) as low risk.

Alex H: repro snippet i ran on a node to mimic load:
```
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -o /dev/null "http://s3.amazonaws.com/bucket/largefile" &
done
# then: netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
#  ~3200 TIME_WAIT
```

ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK: NATGW ephemeral port saturation
- Immediate: add EIPs to NATGW or add additional NATGW in AZ
- Short: enable S3 VPC endpoint and annotate pods for private-s3
- Short: enable egress-proxy sidecar (SOCKS5/http) for model pull namespace
- Medium: implement long-lived HTTP pooling for artifact fetches
- Monitor: CloudWatch MetricFilter: AvailablePorts, PortReuseRate

Julia R: I'll take the VPC endpoint + image pull gating. Plan: create S3 endpoint, annotate daemonset to use endpoint, and patch imagePullPolicy where safe. Stagger node restarts to avoid bursts.

Sam T: I'll stand up a small CANARY proxy (socks5) and flip route for one k8s namespace. If good, we can scale. Started instance, testing now. Early result: per-node TIME_WAITs down ~70% on canary.

Alex H: Owners assigned: @Julia R = endpoint + pull gating (ETA 45m); @Sam T = proxy canary + routing (ETA 30m). If mitigation holds for 2 hours we'll roll to production and create follow up doc.

Julia R: :thumbsup: kicking off now, will post updates here.

Sam T: proxy deployed, smoke tests pass. pushing canary routing. observing reduced NAT allocation pressure.

Alex H: thanks — I'll keep monitoring CloudWatch and conntrack. If we see regression we will add EIPs as emergency. Will create follow-up doc with root cause and long-term fixes (multiplexing, artifact cache).
